canon_constraints.continuity: Star Wars Legends (Expanded Universe), post-Fate of the Jedi, 47 ABY. Crucible (45 ABY) canonical; Legacy comics did NOT happen; the One Sith on Korriban remain in patient pre-emergence under Darth Krayt, glimpsed only as an off-page hand.
canon_constraints.divergence_point: Diverges from published Legends continuity by (a) excising the Legacy comics future entirely — no Darth Krayt galactic war, no Cade Skywalker, no fall of the Galactic Alliance to the One Sith; (b) introducing Aevyn Soris, a marginal Force-sensitive Jedi-rejected at fourteen who joined the GAG as a young adult and became Jacen Solo's side-project Force student during the Caedus period (Ben Skywalker remained Jacen's primary fourteen-year-old apprentice; Aevyn lived in the gaps); (c) introducing Jacen's unfinished holocron — a working device assembled during the LotF period systematizing Recognition, Deepening, and Holding — hidden on Iresh in old GAG-era survey/storage equipment near the Glasswell; (d) introducing the Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation as a legitimate post-war veterans' charity whose hidden inner ring (the Vigil) preserves Jacen-derived 'clarity, resilience, steadiness, preparation' ideology and seeks to recover and finish the holocron.
canon_preserved: Ben Skywalker as Jedi Knight, son of Luke Skywalker and Mara Jade Skywalker; aged ~21 in 47 ABY.
Jacen Solo's fall to Darth Caedus during the Legacy of the Force period and his murder of Mara Jade.
Ben's service in the Galactic Alliance Guard (GAG) under Jacen as a fourteen-year-old, and Ben's later turn against Caedus by the end of the war.
The Abeloth crisis and the broader Fate of the Jedi arc (Daala, Lost Tribe of Sith, Vestara Khai), resolved before Book 1 opens.

Crucible (45 ABY): Luke, Leia, and Han have a transcendent Mortis-adjacent metaphysical encounter; Luke and Leia briefly become luminous beings before being called back; the three emerge changed and effectively retired from active galactic crisis-management work.
The Jedi Order's permanent relocation to Shedu Maad in the Hapes Cluster at the end of FOTJ (44 ABY), after the Senate voted to remove them from Coruscant following the Lost Tribe crisis.
Saba Sebatyne as Grand Master, having assumed the title at the end of FOTJ when Luke stepped down. Luke is a senior Master on the Council, still active, no longer Grand Master.
Wynn Dorvan as Chief of State of the Galactic Alliance, in return-to-normalcy mode after repeated crises (Yuuzhan Vong, Killik, Caedus, Daala, Abeloth, Lost Tribe).
Jagged Fel as Head of State of the Imperial Remnant; Tenel Ka Djo as Queen Mother of Hapes.
Vestara Khai canonically alive and active off-page under the alias 'Savara Raine' as a free-agent dark-side-trained contractor (per Crucible) — never on-page in Book 1.
Tahiri Veila as a Jedi Knight in good standing at Shedu Maad in 47 ABY, Ben's recent working colleague — single passing reference allowed, never as a Caedus reference.
The One Sith on Korriban under Darth Krayt as a real organization in patient pre-emergence, never on-page beyond a single off-page 'hand'.

Jacen Solo's Force odyssey (NJO-LotF transition) as the source-material for his later systematization of Recognition / Deepening / Holding: Vergerean thought; Lumiya's Sith inheritance; experiments performed during the GAG/Caedus period.
Standard Legends Force ontology: light and dark as natural moral-polar properties; Force wounds remain wounds; holocrons as crystalline storage devices for Jedi or Sith teachings.
canon_overridden: Legacy comics continuity (Star Wars: Legacy / Cade Skywalker / Krayt-led galactic war) — entirely excised. The One Sith remain on Korriban in pre-emergence; they do not invade or seize the Galactic Alliance.

Aevyn Soris is a NEW character (not in published Legends): one of Jacen Solo's surviving Force students from the GAG/Caedus period, established as a side project running alongside Jacen's primary apprenticeship of Ben.
The duplicated wartime quarantine/survey shipment manifest personally encrypted by Jacen Solo shortly before the Battle of Shedu Maad is a NEW canonical artifact specific to this novel.

The unfinished holocron's specific contents — Jacen's systematized Recognition, Deepening, and Holding work as identity-shaping technique categories — are this novel's named extrapolation from Jacen's canonical Force-odyssey behavior. Compatible with established Legends; not previously named in published material.

The Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation (public charity), the Vigil (hidden inner ring), Greyline Strategic Services (Tess's firm), and Cinderline (mercenary contractor arm) are NEW post-war Coruscant-political institutions introduced for this novel.

Iresh (remote wind-scoured planet near the edge of known space) and the Glasswell (taboo sinkhole/cavern beneath a mirror-lake, pale translucent mineral) are NEW Outer Rim locations introduced for this novel. Iresh's Force character — preserves charged impressions of memory/identity/decision but does NOT reveal truth or prophecy — is original to this novel and does NOT extend Mortis-adjacent mythology.
Tarn Velos Coastal Detention Works (storm-lashed industrial coastal prison world) and Civitas Archive Systems (Coruscant civic-records restoration and compliance firm) are NEW Book 1 settings.

Allana Solo / Amelia is treated as a dangerous gray zone in adversary awareness only — referenced obliquely in Ch 37 from the Vigil/One Sith POV ('the Hapan question' / 'the unresolved succession thread'). Never named on-page; never enters Ben's awareness. Her identity remains publicly deniable in-universe.
style_constraints: Capitalize 'Human' per Lucasfilm style guide.
Decapitalize 'galaxy' in all contexts unless starting a sentence.
American English spellings throughout.
Star Wars vocabulary discipline: datapads not tablets, transparisteel not glass, durasteel not steel, turbolifts not elevators, comlinks not radios, blasters not guns.
'Jedi' is both singular and plural — never 'Jedis'.
'Darth' as a Sith title is capitalized when preceding a name; generic 'the Sith' lowercase.
Hyperdrive classifications, ship specifications, and planetary names match Wookieepedia entries where existing canon applies.
Do not write theme as thesis. Put theme into behavior, pressure, cost, and consequence.
Do not imitate any specific published Star Wars author's prose. Use broad franchise feel only: cinematic clarity, adventure momentum, lived-in technology, dry humor, mythic Force awe when earned.
Maintain a commercial reader-facing surface at all times: goal, obstacle, movement, reversal, hook.
When in doubt, simplify the metaphysics and clarify the physical action.
Ben should rarely name his fear directly. Other characters' reactions should often reveal it.
Talon's jokes should either move the scene, hide fear, or puncture solemnity. Random quips are not enough.
Aevyn's sympathy should arrive after dread, not before it. Never let Aevyn articulate his wound directly; surface it in fragments — a pause, a sharpness, a way his hand stills.
Sela speaks from local survival knowledge, not Force theory.
Luke is emotionally intelligent, not conveniently fooled. Never have Luke reference 'As Grand Master' for himself — he is no longer Grand Master.
The One Sith remain a background shadow in Book 1 — glimpsed or implied only, never fully revealed.
Emotion shown. Stakes clarified. Jargon minimized. Mystery preserved. Confusion avoided.
The story should always make the current scene goal, immediate obstacle, result, and next danger legible to a Star Wars-aware reader who has not recently read the full Legends timeline.

Explain only what the reader needs for the current emotional or plot decision. Keep exposition packets short (1-3 sentences). Return immediately to action, dialogue, or character reaction. Repeat essential context in different emotional forms rather than dumping it once.

Investigation reader-facing vocabulary stays in physical thriller terms: fragment, duplicate manifest, quarantine disguise, archive, Foundation link, Iresh manifest/authorization. Avoid stacking abstract internal-system labels (no 'routing-index layer', 'black-channel routing grammar', 'stripped transfer shell', 'dead-channel ping', 'transfer node').
No paragraph contains more than one invented bureaucratic/technical term. Every technical phrase translated to immediate human stakes within two sentences.
Avoid 'system' as the default GAG metaphor; prefer logistics network, shipment trail, records chain, transfer chain, or operation.

Use 'Jacen' for the pre-fall identity (mentor / cousin / Force teacher Ben once trusted). Use 'Caedus' for the Sith-Lord identity (the war crimes, the murder of Mara). POV characters choose between them by emotional load: Ben moves between both; Aevyn refuses 'Caedus' and uses 'Jacen' only; Aelia privately thinks of him as Jacen but never publicly defends 'Darth Caedus'; Tess avoids both names in operational dialogue.

GAG = Galactic Alliance Guard. The full name appears once on first use (Ch 1 or Ch 2 narration), abbreviation thereafter. Same convention for the Foundation (Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation, then 'the Foundation').

Crucible aftermath (Luke's post-Mortis state) is implication only — one quiet line of texture in Ch 3 first holo call (tired in a way Ben doesn't remember; eyes further away; longer pauses). Ben notices and does NOT ask. Mortis is never named on-page.

Vestara Khai: mention only (Vara Senn's archive scar-tissue line in Ch 14-15). Vestara is active off-page as 'Savara Raine'; the drafter writes Ben's reaction with the active threat in mind but never makes the resonance explicit on the page.
Tahiri Veila: at most one passing reference if natural; never as a Caedus reference.

Han, Leia, Allana, Jaina: mention only or wholly off-page. Han and Leia are post-Crucible retired; Allana is treated as a dangerous gray zone in adversary awareness only (Ch 37 oblique); Jaina is deliberately excluded.
Mortis monolith / Father-Son-Daughter mythology: not used as plot. The Crucible texture is Luke's unspoken aftermath only; Iresh's Force character is its own simpler thing.

canon_profile.continuity_description: Star Wars Legends EU (pre-April 2014 Expanded Universe). All Legends-published material through Crucible (2013) is valid canon. Anything introduced exclusively in Disney Canon (post-April 2014 sequel trilogy, High Republic initiative, Disney+ original content) is invalid unless it also appeared in Legends sources. Legacy comics (Star Wars: Legacy / Cade Skywalker / Darth Krayt galactic war) are EXCLUDED — the One Sith remain in pre-emergence.
canon_profile.era_description: Post-Abeloth / post-Crucible, 47 ABY in the Legends timeline. Three years after the close of Fate of the Jedi; two years after Crucible. The Galactic Alliance is the ruling galactic government under Chief of State Wynn Dorvan, in return-to-normalcy mode after repeated crises (Yuuzhan Vong, Killik, Second Galactic Civil War / Caedus, Daala, Abeloth, Lost Tribe, Sith occupation/panic). The Jedi Order operates from Shedu Maad in the Hapes Cluster under Grand Master Saba Sebatyne, having relocated permanently from the Coruscant Temple at the end of FOTJ (44 ABY). Luke Skywalker is a senior Master on the Council, stepped back from daily Order leadership after the Mortis-adjacent encounter at Crucible. The Imperial Remnant is stable under Head of State Jagged Fel; Hapes stable under Queen Mother Tenel Ka Djo. Working line: 'The Dorvan administration has restored procedure, not trust.' The galaxy is not healed — it is procedurally stabilized.
canon_profile.narrative_register: Commercial post-war conspiracy thriller in space-opera register. Cinematic clarity, adventure momentum, lived-in technology, dry humor, mythic Force awe when earned. Commercial readability beats literary flourish. The book should read first as a tense Star Wars adventure — murder, prison break, uneasy partnership, archive attack, charity with a hidden inner ring, offworld Force-site climax — and only second as a thematic meditation on Jacen/Caedus, trauma, restraint, and dangerous knowledge. Reader pleasure before theme. The drafter must NOT imitate any specific published Star Wars author's prose; use broad franchise feel only. Reference-author register samples (Allston, Zahn, Traviss, Tana French) anchor sentence-level rhythm and dialogue density, never voice templates.
cross_continuity_violations: Star Wars: Legacy comics (Cade Skywalker, Darth Krayt-led galactic war, fall of the Galactic Alliance to the One Sith). EXCLUDED — the One Sith remain in pre-emergence on Korriban under Darth Krayt.
High Republic (Disney Canon publishing initiative — does not exist in Legends).
World Between Worlds (Disney Canon Force concept from Rebels — incompatible with Legends Force ontology).
Inquisitorius as a formal post-Imperial organization (Disney Canon structure — Legends Inquisitorius is Empire-era only).
Starkiller Base, First Order, Resistance (sequel trilogy — does not exist in Legends).
Kyber crystal bleeding mechanic (Disney Canon lore — Legends Sith use synthetic crystals).
Ahsoka Tano post-Rebels appearances (some Legends material exists but most characterization is Disney Canon).
Disney-canon naming for shared characters (e.g., 'Ben' = Ben Solo). 'Ben' in this novel is unambiguously Ben Skywalker.
Disney-canon Mandalorian visual / political conventions (e.g., 'The Way' as Mandalorian creed — Legends Mandalorians follow Karen Traviss's Resol'nare and post-NJO continuity).
meta_reference_rules: ABY/BBY dating system — fan and sourcebook convention, never used by characters in-universe. Characters reference events directly: 'after Caedus', 'during the Vong War', 'before Shedu Maad', 'two years after we lost Luke at Crucible'.
'Legends' or 'Canon' as terms — these are publishing classifications, not in-universe concepts.
Wookieepedia-style taxonomic descriptions — a character in-universe would not narrate their own species taxonomy.
Referencing 'the prequels', 'the original trilogy', 'the sequel trilogy', or any film/book as a source.
Real-world pop culture references (no '21st-century idioms', no real-world brand names, no internet/meme references).
Out-of-universe authorial framing in narration (no chapter titles invoking real-world songs, films, or book titles; no in-prose narrator addressing the reader directly).
canon_profile.franchise_terminology_notes:
STAR WARS VOCABULARY DISCIPLINE — datapads not tablets, transparisteel not glass, durasteel not steel, turbolifts not elevators, comlinks not radios, blasters not guns, hyperspace not warp, parsecs as distance not time, klicks for short distances.

FORCE PROSE RULE — the Force is rendered through experiential and mystical language, not clinical or scientific framing. Avoid 'energy field' as a description; Luke's generation understands the Force as a living presence, not a measurable phenomenon. Force abilities surface as body-sensations first, named only after the body has felt them.

NAMING DISCIPLINE — 'Jacen' for the pre-fall identity (Ben's cousin, mentor, the boy Mara raised in part); 'Caedus' for the Sith-Lord identity (the war crimes, the murder of Mara). POVs choose by emotional load: Ben slides between both, mostly 'Jacen' when remembering training and 'Caedus' when accusing; Aevyn refuses 'Caedus'; Aelia privately thinks 'Jacen' but never publicly defends 'Darth Caedus'; Tess avoids both names in operational dialogue. Talon uses 'Caedus' when contemptuous, 'Jacen' when Ben is in earshot and he is trying not to wound him.

INSTITUTIONAL NAMES — full name on first use, abbreviation thereafter: Galactic Alliance Guard (GAG); Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation (the Foundation); Greyline Strategic Services (Greyline). 'Cinderline' and 'the Vigil' have no abbreviation. 'Civitas' may stand alone for Civitas Archive Systems after first introduction in Ch 12.

POST-CRUCIBLE TEXTURE — Mortis is NEVER named on-page. One quiet line of texture in Ch 3 (Luke looks tired in a way Ben doesn't remember; eyes further away; longer pauses) is the entire treatment. Ben notices and does NOT ask. A reader who knows Crucible reads it as Mortis aftermath; a reader who does not reads it as a father aging into something new.

INVESTIGATION VOCABULARY — keep reader-facing clue vocabulary in physical-thriller terms: fragment, duplicate manifest, quarantine disguise, archive, Foundation link, Iresh manifest/authorization. Technical GAG/archive language may appear in expert dialogue (Iressa, Talon) for flavor, but every technical phrase translates to a concrete object, danger, location, or next action within two sentences.

force_mechanics.primary_rule: The Force behaves canonically for Legends — light and dark as natural moral-polar properties, Force wounds remain wounds. Iresh and the Glasswell PRESERVE INTENSITY: the planet (and the cavern system beneath the Glasswell's mirror-lake especially) holds charged impressions of memory, identity, and decision under pressure. Iresh does not show the future, reveal objective truth, or grant prophecy. The unfinished holocron is Jacen Solo's private systematization of RECOGNITION, DEEPENING, and HOLDING — identity-shaping techniques aimed at self-perception, recursive self-training, and the preservation of memory/identity/Force-impressions past natural decay. It is part notebook, part training device, part confession, part contingency, part laboratory. It is NOT a completed Sith weapon.
implications: Iresh's Force character is preservation, not revelation. Impressions felt strongly on Iresh are emotionally charged but not objectively reliable. Sela's practical translation: 'Do not trust what you feel here just because it feels strong.'

The Glasswell is a natural site Jacen Solo recognized as useful — a sinkhole/cavern beneath a mirror-lake, lined with pale translucent mineral that holds pressure-impressions unusually well. It is NOT a Sith temple, Jedi ruin, or mystical treasure chamber. The cache itself is hidden in old offworld survey equipment or a concealed GAG-era storage unit embedded near the Glasswell — practical, deniable, Jacen-like.

Forcing the Glasswell to remember the moment Jacen sealed it (as Aevyn does in Ch 30) destabilizes the natural site: water enters, mineral supports crack, survey scaffolds break. The mythic and the physical converge — the cavern's beauty turns to terror through structural failure, not mystical revelation.

Aevyn's Jacen-derived Force-interrogation method (the one that killed Elya Rane in Ch 1) is a weaponized blend of memory pressure, Recognition, and Holding — precise rather than savage. The method extracts memory by forcing the subject's body and mind past survivable limits. The precision is what makes it morally and physically worse than crude torture.

Recognition (the most coherent and potentially useful of the three techniques): tied to self-perception, trauma, memory, and identity-mapping. Used clinically, it could help someone understand who they are. Used coercively, it forces a subject's identity to surface in legible form for the practitioner.

Deepening (promising but dangerous): recursive self-training that can help marginal Force-sensitives grow but risks turning the self into an object of manipulation. This is the technique Aevyn personally benefitted from under Jacen's intermittent attention.

Holding (least complete, most dangerous): concerned with sustaining memory, identity, emotional continuity, and Force-impressions past natural decay. The Vigil's intended use case: identity-level influence on high-value targets — nudging powerful people to experience Sith-favorable choices as their own judgment.

Ben Skywalker can use Force pressure and command in the Jacen-taught way — the GAG-era crisis logic that lets him see panic, exits, timing, and the cost of hesitation in a moment — but refuses to violate another mind. At Ch 14-15 (PP1) he sees a Jacen-shaped coercive move that might save Iressa and chooses not to take it; the line holds and Iressa dies.

Ben's Jacen-derived crisis logic is morally legitimate when it saves lives (Glasswell rescue, Ch 31) and morally dangerous when it persuades the user that his most defensible choice is also his most expensive one. The novel does NOT settle which is which; that is the thematic argument.

Aevyn's self-built lightsaber emits a cold white-blue blade that shivers along the edge, crackles faintly under pressure, fractures into small white-blue forks when his control strains, and becomes more unstable when he is emotionally pressed. The instability is the work of a competent man who was never formally trained in lightsaber construction or form — combat instinct from GAG plus Force exercises from Jacen, no tradition to bridge them. During the Ch 31-32 duel, the blade fractures MORE visibly when Ben successfully uses Jacen-derived logic — a visual tell, NOT exposition. Aevyn registers Ben as Jacen's primary student through the blade's behavior before either of them speaks the fact.

Vara Senn's dark-side Force methods are crude — pressure, fear, domination — and are explicitly framed as the Lost Tribe lineage. They are intentionally cruder than Aevyn's; Vara is the warning shot, Aevyn is the mirror. Ben recognizes Lost Tribe footwork during the Ch 14-15 archive clash, allowing a brief Vestara Khai scar-tissue beat without bringing Vestara on-page.

Crucible aftermath: Luke is post-Mortis-encounter and stepped back from active galactic crisis-management work. On Mortis-adjacent metaphysical content — never named on-page — Luke is quieter than he used to be, his eyes look tired in a way Ben doesn't quite remember, his pauses are longer. This texture is implication only, lifted from the Crucible novel by Troy Denning; the drafter must NOT explain it on the page.

The One Sith on Korriban under Darth Krayt remain in patient pre-emergence. Their Book 1 footprint is one off-page 'hand' that learns Iresh failed in Ch 37 and adjusts the broader infiltration program. The unfinished holocron's value to them is the identity-shaping potential of Recognition / Deepening / Holding seeded into future high-value targets (Wynn Dorvan as eventual target, never compromised in Book 1).

Holocron canon (Legends standard): crystalline storage devices imprinted with Force resonance to preserve teachings, exercises, and the personality of the keeper. Holocrons can be Jedi-aligned or Sith-aligned. Jacen's holocron is anomalous because it is UNFINISHED — a work-in-progress assembled from heterogeneous sources, opened by exercise-driven engagement rather than gatekeeper-test, capable of being used by a marginal Force-sensitive (Aevyn) with the right method.
force_mechanics.canon_grounding: Builds on established Legends precedents: Jacen Solo's Force odyssey across the New Jedi Order / Dark Nest / Legacy of the Force novels; Vergerean thought (Yuuzhan'tar / Ossus monastery exposure); Lumiya's Sith inheritance (LotF: Bloodlines, Sacrifice); Jacen's GAG-era experiments documented across LotF; Crucible (2013) Mortis-adjacent encounter for Luke/Leia/Han's post-active state; Fate of the Jedi (Outcast through Apocalypse) for the Order's relocation to Shedu Maad and Saba Sebatyne's ascension to Grand Master; standard Legends holocron canon (Tales of the Jedi, KOTOR-era references, Dark Empire). The named Recognition / Deepening / Holding categories, Aevyn Soris as Jacen's surviving student, the unfinished holocron's Iresh-cache placement, the duplicated wartime quarantine manifest, and the Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation / Vigil / Greyline / Cinderline are original era-language and infrastructure layered onto those canon foundations — not proof of new universal ontology. Iresh's preservation-of-impressions character extrapolates from FOTJ / Crucible vergence-and-lore-site lineage but does NOT extend Mortis-adjacent mythology; Iresh is its own simpler thing.

terminology_registry.definition: Protagonist. Jedi Knight, age ~21 in 47 ABY. Son of Luke Skywalker and Mara Jade Skywalker. Briefly apprenticed to Jacen Solo as a fourteen-year-old; served in the Galactic Alliance Guard under Jacen; turned against Caedus by the end of the war. Lost Mara to Jacen/Caedus. Categorized by family as victim, by Order as survivor; neither category fully honest.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Talon calls him 'Skywalker' when guarded, 'Ben' when trust slips through. Sela calls him 'Skywalker' through Ch 28, then 'Ben' from Ch 34 onward. Aevyn calls him 'Ben Skywalker' — full name, never shortened — because the full name is the wound.

terminology_registry.definition: Co-protagonist / partner. 28, human, Coruscanti. Former GAG field agent turned black-channel logistics/security officer; imprisoned at Tarn Velos at story start. Was Colonel Maro Tess's protégé until Operation Glasshook; was reassigned into logistics/records after disobeying Tess to save trapped civilians. The reassignment became the record that ruined him.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Tess calls him 'Talon' — first name — with proprietary calm; Talon hates it. Korda's 'Veyr. I assumed they had better locks.' is the only line where Korda uses his surname.

terminology_registry.definition: True mirror antagonist. 28, human. Jacen Solo's surviving Force student from the GAG/Caedus period. Marginal Force-sensitive politely rejected by the Jedi at fourteen at a regional outreach office; later joined GAG as a young adult as a field analyst / operations specialist before the Caedus period; Jacen found him there and treated him as a side project while Ben remained the primary fourteen-year-old apprentice. Wields a self-built unstable cold white-blue lightsaber.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Aevyn refuses to call Jacen 'Caedus' — uses 'Jacen' only. The corridor flashback wound-image (Jacen leaving a session with Aevyn to walk off with young Ben) surfaces as fragment in his Act 3 POV — NEVER as exposition or speech. Aevyn presumed dead at Glasswell collapse; cold white-blue spark in Ch 38 confirms survival to the reader only.

terminology_registry.definition: Operational antagonist. Late forties, ~49. Former senior GAG operations officer; current Greyline Strategic Services strategist; operational architect for the Vigil; knowing One Sith asset. Was Talon Veyr's senior commander and mentor figure during the war; reassigned Talon out of field duty after Operation Glasshook. Believes power is real, hesitation kills, and morality is usually written after control has been secured.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Survives Book 1 and retreats deeper into One Sith service in Ch 37. NO villain poetry — Tess speaks operationally, like a man who sorts lives into categories. Treats failures as logistics.

terminology_registry.definition: Public-face antagonist. Late fifties, human. Executive Director of the Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation. Former Senate staffer and widow from the Second Galactic Civil War. Warm, polished, prepared, genuinely compassionate, dangerous because much of what she says is true. Writes condolence notes by hand; remembers scholarship recipients' names; never publicly defends 'Darth Caedus'. Steps down in public disgrace in Ch 35 to preserve the Foundation's legitimate charitable work; no criminal liability.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Privately thinks of Jacen as Jacen, never as Caedus. Beats Ben SOCIALLY at the Ch 17 Foundation visit before she is exposed operationally.

terminology_registry.definition: Foundation security director. Early forties, human. Old GAG security lieutenant in respectable clothing. Director of Protective Services for the Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation; privately coordinates Foundation logistics with old GAG-linked security and mercenary contractors. Talon knew him during GAG and disliked him.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Killed/discarded by Tess in PP2 (Ch 20) as the public fall guy for the conspiracy's exposed crimes. Smooth with superiors, cruel through process, never openly messy when witnesses matter.

terminology_registry.definition: Short-arc Act 2 ally. Human or near-human (possibly Kiffar-descended without making psychometry a major plot feature). Former GAG Manifest Integrity Analyst; current senior records-restoration analyst at Civitas Archive Systems. Specialized in wartime cargo discrepancies, duplicate manifests, quarantine classifications, restricted transfer corrections. Charges Ben a 'Jedi complication fee' on first meeting. Renamed from working name 'Mira Vossk' in v8.3 to avoid name collision with Mara.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Dies at the GAG archive in Ch 15 actively denying Vara Senn a clean copy and transmitting the two-part dying package (documentary chain + identity-shaping revelation) to Ben and Talon. Old Iressa buried discrepancies; new Iressa preserves one.

terminology_registry.definition: Warning-shot dark-side contractor. Former Lost Tribe of Sith apprentice now doing mercenary work. Dangerous but undisciplined; sells Force talent to clients who pay late and resents the indignity. Uses pressure, fear, and domination — crude dark-side contrast to Aevyn's refined Jacen-derived method.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Engages Ben in a short ugly lightsaber clash at the Ch 14-15 archive cleanup, then takes Iressa hostage when combat doesn't work. Drops a brief Vestara Khai mention as scar-tissue test. Disappears into the contractor pool after the archive; does NOT return on-page in Book 1. Book 2 seed.

terminology_registry.definition: Iresh local guide / settlement liaison. Early thirties, human or near-human. Knows weather, paths, taboo ground, chime-lines, and what offworlders break when they arrive with causes. Dislikes Ben and Talon as offworlders but recognizes they may be the only tools available to stop worse offworlders. Survives Book 1.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Refuses Force theory; speaks in survival rules. Saves Tavi and locals through local knowledge Ben does NOT have — distinct climax job. Calls Ben 'Skywalker' through Ch 28; shifts to 'Ben' from Ch 34 onward, conditional trust only.

terminology_registry.definition: Sela's younger relative / apprentice figure. Iresh local pressured/paid by the Foundation into the Glasswell zone as a guide. Younger, practical, overconfident, loved. Trapped below during Aevyn's forced opening of the Glasswell cache; rescued by Ben's Jacen-shaped crisis logic at Ch 31; imperfect reunion with Sela in Ch 34.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Tavi must be PRESENT before he is endangered — seeded through a carved guide-token, field recorder, local guide marks, prior warning, or a child/family member asking after him.

terminology_registry.definition: Opening victim and normal-person history lens. Former GAG records/logistics officer. Discovers the duplicated wartime quarantine/survey shipment manifest in Ch 1 and contacts Ben through an obsolete GAG-coded channel because she once quietly removed Ben's name from a wrong approval field when he was fourteen. Murdered by Aevyn through Jacen-derived Force-interrogation.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: POV of Ch 1 in full through her death. Should be briefly competent, afraid, and human before the plot kills her. The fragment she preserved survives beyond what Aevyn extracts.

terminology_registry.definition: Senior Master of the Jedi Order, Ben's father. No longer Grand Master (Saba Sebatyne assumed the title at the end of FOTJ). Based at Shedu Maad through the novel; communicates with Ben on Coruscant by holo. Post-Crucible state: quieter, eyes further away, longer pauses — implication only, Mortis never named.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Three Book 1 conversations: Ch 3 first holo call (paternal advice, classify the matter as sensitive but not catastrophic); Ch 16 Midpoint paternal+institutional call (directs Ben to Saba); Ch 20 brief PP2 second holo call from the Skywalker apartment (Luke understands what Ben has decided, does not try to stop him). Ch 36 is the first in-person exchange since the holo calls — the 'Gone where?' coda. NEVER use 'As Grand Master, I must...' — he is no longer Grand Master.

terminology_registry.definition: Ben's mother. Murdered by Jacen Solo during the LotF / Second Galactic Civil War period. Appears in Book 1 only as memory, family-holo presence, and Ben's emotional wound. Has not been seen on-page (alive) since LotF: Sacrifice.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Mentions of Mara are a vulnerability point for Ben — they should feel earned, not used as cheap emotional levers. The Ch 11 Skywalker apartment beat surfaces her absence through a preserved family holo, not through dialogue or memory exposition.

terminology_registry.definition: Pre-fall identity. Ben's cousin, mentor, and Force teacher during the GAG / Caedus period. Son of Han Solo and Leia Organa Solo; brother of Jaina. Killed at the Battle of Shedu Maad in 40 ABY. His Force odyssey (NJO through LotF) produced the Vergerean / Lumiya-inflected techniques he later systematized as Recognition, Deepening, and Holding in the unfinished holocron.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Naming discipline: 'Jacen' for the pre-fall mentor identity, 'Caedus' for the Sith-Lord identity. POVs choose by emotional load — see canon_profile.franchise_terminology_notes. Aevyn ONLY uses 'Jacen'.

terminology_registry.definition: Sith-Lord identity of Jacen Solo during the LotF Second Galactic Civil War. Architect of the Galactic Alliance Guard's wartime excesses, murder of Mara Jade Skywalker, killed at the Battle of Shedu Maad. References in Book 1 are emotionally loaded; the name appears in narration when the speaker means the war-crimes identity, not the mentor.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Aelia NEVER publicly defends 'Darth Caedus' — civic, memorial, therapeutic language only. Aevyn REFUSES 'Caedus'. Tess avoids both names in operational dialogue.

terminology_registry.definition: Grand Master of the Jedi Order. Barabel. Assumed the title at the end of Fate of the Jedi when Luke Skywalker stepped down. Measured, fierce when needed, committed to bringing institutional stability to an Order that has been through too many crises. Based at Shedu Maad.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Appears in one Ch 16 holo call from Ben (institutional report after Iressa's death). Speaks with Barabel gravity — careful, sharp questions, formal review register. The slowness of her correct review process is the institutional pressure that forces Ben's Midpoint pivot; Saba is NOT the villain.

terminology_registry.definition: Chief of State of the Galactic Alliance circa 47 ABY. Quiet, competent, careful — restoring procedure after repeated crises. NOT brainwashed or mind-controlled in Book 1. Future high-value target in a broader One Sith identity-shaping infiltration program, not yet a Book 1 puppet.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Mentioned only as context for the Dorvan administration's 'return to normalcy' political register. The unnamed One Sith hand in Ch 37 considers Dorvan as a future target.

terminology_registry.definition: Head of State of the Imperial Remnant. Stable post-FOTJ. Brief reference only.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: No on-page appearance. Mentioned only to establish the post-FOTJ galactic state.

terminology_registry.definition: Queen Mother of Hapes. Allana Solo's mother. Stable post-FOTJ on the Hapan throne; Jedi-trained.

terminology_registry.definition: Former Lost Tribe apprentice; canonically alive and active off-page under the alias 'Savara Raine' as a free-agent dark-side-trained contractor per Crucible (45 ABY). Ben's prior love interest who chose the dark side. NOT in Book 1 beyond scar-tissue mention.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Vara Senn drops Vestara's name during the Ch 14-15 archive clash to test whether the name still lands. The drafter knows the canonical Vestara is currently OUT THERE doing things; write Ben's reaction with active threat in mind but never make the resonance explicit on the page.

terminology_registry.definition: Jedi Knight in good standing at Shedu Maad in 47 ABY. Per Crucible, served alongside Ben to rescue Luke and Leia from the Qrephs. Ben's recent working colleague.

terminology_registry.definition: Effectively retired post-Crucible. Off-page in Book 1.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Mention only — never on-page. Han and Leia are with family, possibly at Shedu Maad or elsewhere.

terminology_registry.definition: Effectively retired post-Crucible. Off-page in Book 1. Should be told enough to feel the Caedus resonance, but not brought into the conspiracy plot.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Mention only — never on-page. The novel does not bring her into the Vigil investigation.

terminology_registry.definition: Daughter of Tenel Ka Djo and Jacen Solo, hidden as 'Amelia Solo' under Han and Leia's guardianship per FOTJ. Publicly deniable; suspected/known by some. Treated as a dangerous gray zone in Book 1 — referenced obliquely in Ch 37 (Tess / One Sith hand POV) as 'the Hapan question' or similar; never named on-page, never enters Ben's awareness.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: HARD CONSTRAINT: never named on-page. The Ch 37 reference is the only acknowledgement that the Vigil has clocked her existence. The Hapan-line phrasing should be specific enough that a Legends-aware reader recognizes her and a new reader sees one more unfinished asset on the adversary's desk.

terminology_registry.definition: Jacen Solo's twin sister. Effectively retired or out-of-frame in Book 1. Deliberately excluded — bringing her into the Vigil investigation would be using her grief.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: HARD CONSTRAINT: not in Book 1. No on-page appearance, no mention beyond at most a single passing reference if absolutely needed.

terminology_registry.definition: Leader of the One Sith on Korriban. In patient pre-emergence; never on-page in Book 1. The Legacy-comics future where Krayt led a galactic war against the Galactic Alliance does NOT happen in this continuity.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: HARD CONSTRAINT: never on-page. Referenced only as 'the hand' or 'the long game' in Ch 37 from Tess or the One Sith hand's perspective.

terminology_registry.definition: Galactic Alliance capital world. Anchors Acts 1-2 of the novel. The Jedi Order has NO institutional foothold here in 47 ABY — the Coruscant Jedi Temple was relinquished at the end of FOTJ (44 ABY) after the Senate voted to remove the Order following the Lost Tribe crisis. The Skywalker family apartment is the last Skywalker presence on a world that pushed the Order out.

Remote wind-scoured world near the edge of known space. Anchors Act 3. Pale mineral cliffs; cold highlands; dark water; black reed marshes; thin forests; long winds; wind-carved stone arches; shallow mirror-lakes; stacked stone path-markers; metal chimes / wind markers; thin aurora-like veils in the sky. Iresh's Force character: preserves charged impressions of memory, identity, and decision under pressure. Does NOT reveal truth or prophecy.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Iresh is a place BEFORE it is a metaphor. Every Act 3 chapter must include at least one grounding anchor (weather / terrain / local custom / physical danger / Sela's practical knowledge / Tavi's human stake / clear spatial geography). The Force atmosphere rides on top of that, not in place of it.

terminology_registry.definition: Taboo cavern/sinkhole system on Iresh, located beneath a mirror-lake and lined with pale translucent mineral that holds pressure-impressions unusually well. The cache hiding Jacen Solo's unfinished holocron is concealed near the Glasswell in old offworld survey equipment or a GAG-era storage unit — practical, deniable, Jacen-like. Local phrase: 'Some places remember too loudly.'
terminology_registry.usage_notes: NOT a Sith temple, Jedi ruin, or mystical treasure chamber. The cavern's geography MUST be physically clear before it collapses in Ch 30-32 (mirror-lake above; sinkhole below; pale mineral walls; survey scaffold; cache embedded in survey/GAG equipment; lower ledge where Tavi is trapped; one main path out; one dangerous water route).

terminology_registry.definition: Hapes Cluster world where the Jedi Order relocated permanently at the end of FOTJ (44 ABY) and where the Order still maintains its headquarters in 47 ABY. The Battle of Shedu Maad (40 ABY) was where Darth Caedus was killed at the close of LotF.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Pronounced SHEH-doo MAHD. The Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation takes its name from the post-war reconstruction of the battle's losses.

terminology_registry.definition: Star cluster on the borders of the Inner Rim, ruled by the Hapan Consortium under Queen Mother Tenel Ka Djo. Houses Shedu Maad and the Jedi Order's current headquarters.

Storm-lashed industrial coastal prison world where Talon Veyr is held at story start. Features: sea-wall system, waste runoff systems, gantries, storm shutters, camera lag, maintenance habits. Setting of the Ch 6-9 prison sequence including the FPP storm-line escape.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: The prison must be a physical action environment, not a generic prison. Wind, rain, sea spray, cold metal, storm sound through the walls — sensory anchors throughout the sequence.

terminology_registry.definition: Coruscant civic-records restoration and compliance firm. Repairs damaged public records, casualty files, displacement registries, charity/government archive errors, and legacy war database inconsistencies. Iressa Vossk's respectable cover employer. Setting of the Ch 12 introduction including the Civitas lunchroom small-talk beat.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Civitas must feel like a real workplace before it becomes the wound: ordinary coworkers, mundane office politics, painfully normal small talk about caf and record migrations.

terminology_registry.definition: Memorial chamber in the Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation's headquarters. Publicly a place for names, lights, personal tokens, and grief rituals. After hours, the Vigil's meeting place.

Skywalker family residence on Coruscant. The last Skywalker presence on the world that pushed the Order out at the end of FOTJ. Preserved family holo (Mara, Luke, young Ben) on a shelf; Luke's quiet stack of old mission logs. Used as one-night supply stop in Ch 11; becomes Ben and Talon's final refuge for the PP2 run-up to Iresh.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: A human breather, not a nostalgia shrine. Two objects only carry weight (the family holo + Luke's mission logs). The Ch 11 and Ch 20+ visits must feel like different beats — first a brush past the wound, then a return to it.

terminology_registry.definition: Sith homeworld in the Outer Rim. Home of the One Sith in patient pre-emergence under Darth Krayt. Never on-page in Book 1; mentioned only as the long-game shadow behind Tess's operation.

The ruling galactic polity in 47 ABY. Chief of State: Wynn Dorvan. Successor to the New Republic after the Yuuzhan Vong War. In return-to-normalcy mode after repeated crises. Working line: 'The Dorvan administration has restored procedure, not trust.'

Headquartered at Shedu Maad (Hapes Cluster) under Grand Master Saba Sebatyne, having relocated permanently from the Coruscant Temple at the end of FOTJ (44 ABY). Luke Skywalker is a senior Master on the Council, stepped back after Crucible.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: The Order has NO institutional foothold on Coruscant in 47 ABY. This matters for the novel: Ben is operating on a planet where the Jedi have no base, no resources, no political cover.

terminology_registry.definition: Wartime security force from the Second Galactic Civil War (LotF era) that became morally corrupt under Jacen Solo's command. Dissolved in disgrace after Shedu Maad. The afterlife of GAG — its records, its survivors, its hidden logistics network — is the novel's central conspiracy substrate.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Full name on first use, 'GAG' thereafter. The novel's GAG history is shown through PERSONAL CONSEQUENCES — files, names, fields, euphemisms, small moral choices — not as a lore lecture.

terminology_registry.definition: Legitimate post-war veterans' and war-families charity formed after the Second Galactic Civil War and the Battle of Shedu Maad. Public work: scholarships for children of GA service members; grief counseling; casualty-record preservation; legal/benefits advocacy; memorial events; veteran networking; grants to local war memorials. Most members and staff are innocent. Aelia Vandros is Executive Director.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Full name on first use, 'the Foundation' thereafter. The public charitable work is REAL — Ben cannot morally flatten the organization without losing.

terminology_registry.definition: The Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation's hidden inner ring. Began as a private donor/remembrance circle for families who believed the official postwar story left too much buried. Became the ideological core preserving Jacen-derived work. Belief: the galaxy keeps nearly dying because leaders hesitate, panic, compromise, or wait too long; Jacen failed but saw something real. Language: clarity, resilience, steadiness, correction, continuity, moral courage, preparation. NOT 'brainwashing'.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: The Vigil's language is civic and therapeutic, never theological or theatrical. Members do not call themselves Sith and do not publicly defend Caedus.

terminology_registry.definition: Colonel Maro Tess's private security firm. Publicly provides donor-event security, archive protection, offworld survey security, threat assessments, personnel vetting, hostile-environment logistics, and private protection for charities/civic institutions. Privately serves as the Vigil's operational arm.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Full name on first use, 'Greyline' thereafter. Greyline's contractor arm for direct action is Cinderline.

terminology_registry.definition: Mercenary contractor arm Greyline uses for direct action (snatch operations, archive cleanups, frame-ups, asset disposals). The Vigil's plausibly-deniable muscle. Executes the Tarn Velos prison snatch (PP1 prelude), the GAG archive cleanup (PP1), the cache raid and Talon frame (PP2), and the Iresh staging.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Cinderline operations are professional and procedural — frame-ups, false-cover snatches, professional cache destructions. NOT crude or theatrical.

terminology_registry.definition: The successor state of the Galactic Empire, stable under Head of State Jagged Fel in 47 ABY. Off-page in Book 1.

Sith order discovered and engaged during the Fate of the Jedi arc. Largely scattered and broken by 47 ABY. Vara Senn is a former apprentice now doing mercenary work; Vestara Khai is canonically active off-page under the alias 'Savara Raine'.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Mentioned in Book 1 only as scar tissue and Vara Senn's institutional origin. Not an active organizational antagonist in this novel.

terminology_registry.definition: The Sith order on Korriban under Darth Krayt, in patient pre-emergence in 47 ABY. The Vigil is a client / asset of the One Sith's broader identity-shaping infiltration program. In Book 1 the One Sith appear only as a single off-page 'hand' that learns Iresh failed in Ch 37 and adjusts the program.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: HARD CONSTRAINT: the One Sith are glimpsed or implied only. The hand has no name in Book 1.

terminology_registry.definition: Pre-Reformations Sith order. Background reference only in this novel — mentioned in conjunction with general Sith historiography or Aevyn's reading of Sith lineage. Not relevant to Book 1 plot.

An unfinished working holocron assembled during the Legacy of the Force period from fragments of Jacen Solo's Force-odyssey notes, Vergerean thought, Lumiya's Sith inheritance, GAG-era observations, and Jacen's private systematization of Recognition, Deepening, and Holding. Part notebook, part training device, part confession, part contingency, part laboratory. Hidden on Iresh near the Glasswell in old offworld survey / GAG-era storage equipment.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: NOT a completed Sith weapon. Reader-facing language treats it as 'Jacen's notebook on how to shape people from the inside, and the Vigil wants to finish the work.' Ben secures it in Ch 33 and preserves it through the coda — his omission to Luke in Ch 36 is technically true and morally incomplete.

terminology_registry.canonical_form: the duplicated wartime quarantine/survey shipment manifest
terminology_registry.definition: A duplicated wartime quarantine/survey shipment manifest from the final days before the Battle of Shedu Maad. One version is public and boring; the hidden duplicate carries the same shipment identity, a quarantine/survey disguise, conflicting destination data, and enough metadata to show Jacen Solo personally encrypted it shortly before his death. The opening clue chain.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Reader-facing question is simple: 'Why did one of Jacen's last shipments have two lives?' The fragment Ben recovers from Elya's murder scene in Ch 4 is the DAMAGED clean copy; Iressa Vossk reconstructs around Jacen's encryption to prove the lie. Investigation vocabulary stays in physical terms — fragment, duplicate manifest, quarantine disguise, archive.

terminology_registry.definition: Self-built lightsaber Aevyn Soris assembled during his postwar pilgrimage from salvaged components, a crystal found outside the Jedi tradition, and focusing adjustments derived from Jacen Solo's unfinished notes. Cold white-blue blade. Shivers along the edge. Crackles faintly under pressure. Fractures into small white-blue forks when his control strains. Becomes more unstable when he is emotionally pressed.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: NOT red and NOT obviously Sith-coded. The instability is the work of a competent man who was never formally trained in lightsaber construction or form. Visual TELL — during the Ch 31-32 duel the blade fractures MORE visibly when Ben successfully uses Jacen-derived logic. NEVER expose this in exposition or dialogue; let the image do the work.

terminology_registry.definition: Iressa Vossk's off-record reconstruction workshop, separate from Civitas Archive Systems. A quiet leased space in a Coruscant records-warehouse district (or basement workshop / sympathetic-small-business backroom — drafter's choice). Houses the old GAG tools, encrypted dead drops, and personal archive instincts she officially renounced. Not connected to Civitas or her residence in any public record. Where Ben and Talon spend several days continuing reconstruction after Iressa's death. RAIDED AND BURNED by Cinderline at PP2 (Ch 20) — the documentary case for Saba becomes unrecoverable.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Established in Ch 13 as a passing detail — one line, no emphasis. Becomes the target of PP2's first beat. The raid happens OFF-SCREEN for Ben; he arrives after, and the loss lands through the destroyed space, not through action.

terminology_registry.definition: A GAG record from the wartime period that would have made fourteen-year-old Ben Skywalker look more responsible for an ugly authorization chain than he truly was. Commander Elya Rane quietly removed Ben's name from this approval field — not because she loved the Jedi or because she was heroic, but because even inside GAG she thought someone should remember Ben was a child. The small human correction that connects Elya to Ben personally and motivates her Ch 1 message.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Pay it off in Ch 2 (Ben remembering it before opening the message) and Ch 4 (after the murder, the weight of why she contacted him specifically).

terminology_registry.definition: Working name for the wartime GAG interdiction mission on Coruscant during which Talon Veyr disobeyed Colonel Maro Tess's order to stay on a high-value courier/data asset, diverting the extraction route to save trapped civilians and GA personnel at the cost of the mission. Tess reassigned Talon out of field duty as punishment/'education', intending to teach him to see the whole operation rather than only the people in front of him. The reassignment became the record that ruined Talon.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: The defining wound between Talon and Tess. Surfaces in dialogue in Ch 22 ('He said field work had made me sentimental. Logistics would teach me scale.' / 'Did it?' / 'It taught me how easy it is to lose people in paperwork.').

terminology_registry.definition: GAG wartime operation referenced in Talon's history (Ch 22). Less developed than Glasshook; a name only, used to extend the texture of Talon's wartime experience without committing to a specific incident.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Flavor reference only — no plot weight. Drafter may invent texture for a single line if needed.

terminology_registry.definition: Aevyn Soris's specific wound-image. Aevyn at a side console running a Recognition exercise Jacen Solo had given him, Jacen actually present and watching/correcting; fourteen-year-old Ben coming down the corridor; Jacen looking up, saying 'Good. Keep going. We'll review later,' and walking off with Ben. The 'later' never came. The single sharpest character detail in the project.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Surfaces as a fragment in Aevyn's Act 3 POV — a brief, controlled flash that breaks through when he confronts Ben. NEVER as exposition. NEVER as speech. Just the corridor, Jacen turning, Ben walking past.

terminology_registry.definition: The most coherent and potentially useful of Jacen Solo's three systematized identity-shaping techniques. Tied to self-perception, trauma, memory, and identity-mapping. Used clinically, it could help someone understand who they are; used coercively, it forces a subject's identity to surface in legible form for the practitioner. The technique Aevyn was running when the corridor moment fractured his attention with Jacen.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Capitalized when used as the technique's proper name; lowercase 'recognition' for ordinary uses of the English word. Distinguish carefully in narration.

terminology_registry.definition: The second of Jacen Solo's three systematized techniques. Recursive self-training. Promising but dangerous: can help marginal Force-sensitives grow but risks turning the self into an object of manipulation. The technique Aevyn personally benefited from under Jacen's intermittent attention.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Capitalized when used as the technique's proper name.

terminology_registry.definition: The third and least complete of Jacen Solo's three systematized techniques. Concerned with sustaining memory, identity, emotional continuity, and Force-impressions past natural decay. The most dangerous of the three. The Vigil's intended weaponized use case: identity-level influence on high-value targets — nudging powerful people to experience Sith-favorable choices as their own judgment.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Capitalized when used as the technique's proper name. The Holding technique is what makes Jacen's unfinished holocron strategically valuable to the One Sith.

terminology_registry.definition: Aevyn Soris's weaponized Force-interrogation method. A precise blend of memory pressure, Recognition, and Holding. Kills by pushing the subject's mind and body past survivable limits. The precision is what makes it morally and physically worse than crude torture — it forces the subject's memories into clarity rather than fragmenting them.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Used to kill Elya Rane in Ch 1 (off-screen of the extraction; on-screen of the death) and used to pressure Iressa Vossk's secondary cache and identity in Vara's hostage attempt in Ch 14-15 (which fails — Vara is not Aevyn, and her cruder version reaches its limit before extraction completes).

terminology_registry.definition: Not a Force technique — a mindset Jacen Solo taught Ben Skywalker during the GAG year. How to see panic, timing, exits, the whole room, and the cost of hesitation in a moment. Surfaces in Ben's behavior subtly throughout Book 1 and decisively during the Glasswell rescue (Ch 31), where it saves Tavi, Sela's locals, and others. The lesson Aevyn recognizes when Ben uses it: 'He taught you that.'
terminology_registry.usage_notes: The most legible Jacen-lesson the novel can show. Ben experiences it as discomfort with his own competence; other characters see it before he names it. The drafter must show, not name, until late.

terminology_registry.definition: Star Wars Legends dating convention: years counted from the Battle of Yavin (the destruction of the first Death Star). Used in sourcebooks and out-of-universe reference. NEVER used by characters in-universe — characters reference events directly ('after Caedus', 'two years after Crucible').
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Background convention only. Appears in canon documentation, never in narration or dialogue.

terminology_registry.definition: Sentient bipedal species, the most numerically dominant in the galaxy. Capitalized per Lucasfilm style guide.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Always capitalized. Most main characters are Human (Ben, Talon, Aevyn, Tess, Aelia, Korda, Elya, Vara).

terminology_registry.definition: Reptilian species native to Barab I. Known for keen senses, gravity-dense culture, and martial directness. Grand Master Saba Sebatyne is Barabel.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Saba's speech register carries Barabel gravity — careful, sharp, formal. Some Barabel speech patterns use 'this one' for self-reference; the drafter may apply this sparingly.

terminology_registry.definition: Near-Human species from Kiffu and Kiffex. Some Kiffar possess psychometry (the ability to read impressions from objects through touch). Iressa Vossk may be Kiffar-descended, but the novel does NOT make psychometry a major plot feature.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Iressa's exact heritage is flexible — drafter may keep her Human or render her as Kiffar-descended at their discretion. Psychometry stays off-page if used.

terminology_registry.definition: Standard rank within the Jedi Order, achieved after the trials. Ben Skywalker holds this rank.
Senior rank within the Jedi Order, granted by Council elevation in recognition of teaching and judgment.
Informal designation for Masters of recognized standing on the Council. Luke Skywalker holds this position post-Crucible.
Leader of the Jedi Order. Saba Sebatyne holds this title in 47 ABY, having assumed it at the end of FOTJ when Luke Skywalker stepped down.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Luke never references the title for himself. When characters address Saba, use 'Grand Master' formally; 'Saba' informally only for those with the standing (Luke, perhaps a small number of Masters).

terminology_registry.definition: Senior GAG operations rank. Maro Tess held this rank during the war and continues to be addressed as such by Talon and others who knew him then.
Senior GAG records/logistics rank. Elya Rane held this rank during and after the war.
Aelia Vandros's title at the Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation.
Bren Korda's title at the Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation.
Head of the Galactic Alliance executive. Wynn Dorvan holds this position in 47 ABY.
Reigning monarch of the Hapan Consortium. Tenel Ka Djo holds this position in 47 ABY.
Leader of the Imperial Remnant. Jagged Fel holds this position in 47 ABY.

Plasma-blade weapon constructed around a focusing crystal, the traditional weapon of the Jedi and Sith. Color varies by crystal source and tradition. Ben Skywalker's blade is Jedi-standard; Aevyn's is a self-built unstable cold white-blue.

Crystalline storage device imprinted with Force resonance to preserve teachings, exercises, and the personality of the keeper. Can be Jedi-aligned or Sith-aligned. Jacen Solo's holocron is anomalous because it is UNFINISHED — see 'the unfinished holocron'.
Personal communication device. Standard equipment for civilian and military use.
Portable computing/display device. Replaces 'tablet' or 'laptop' in all in-prose use.

Three-dimensional projection technology — used for communication (holo call), entertainment (holovid), and imagery (preserved family holo). Ben's communication with Luke during the novel is by holo call.
Galaxy-wide communications and broadcast network. The medium for news coverage of the Foundation scandal in Ch 35.
Faster-than-light travel medium. Standard Star Wars FTL convention; ships make jumps via hyperdrive.
The propulsion system that allows ships to travel through hyperspace. Classifications follow Legends conventions.
Liquid healing medium used to treat wounds and burns. Standard Legends medical convention; characters with injuries spend time in bacta after the Ch 7 prison escape and the Ch 31-32 climax.
Light atmospheric craft used for short transport. Talon and Ben extract from Tarn Velos by skiff/shuttle in Ch 9.
Transparent armor-grade material used for ship viewports and high-rise windows. Replaces 'glass' in in-prose use.
Standard high-strength alloy. Replaces 'steel' in in-prose use.

Iresh local custom — wind-chime arrays strung along paths to warn locals when wind patterns shift dangerously. Sela Dray repairs a chime line during her introduction in Ch 24. Chimes going silent is a warning sign in Iresh's local survival vocabulary.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Sela's example survival rule: 'If the chimes stop, run. You can argue about what it means after you are not dead.'

terminology_registry.definition: Iresh marsh flora. Forms dense dark stands along the lower paths near the Glasswell exclusion zone. Crossing them after the chimes stop is one of Sela's named survival prohibitions.

Iresh local convention — stacked stone markers indicating safe routes through wind-carved highlands and marsh. The Foundation/Vigil's offworld survey crews have removed some markers because they 'interfered with equipment' — one of the visible local harms.
Iresh geographic feature — shallow lakes whose still surfaces reflect the highlands. The Glasswell sinkhole opens directly beneath one such mirror-lake.

The Galactic Alliance's judicial/legal enforcement arm. Ben uses a low-profile GA Justice records-auditor cover to enter Tarn Velos in Ch 6. Luke calls in quiet favors with GA Justice contacts during the Ch 10 aftermath of the prison escape.

The post-Yuuzhan Vong era war (40-41 ABY) that produced Jacen Solo's fall to Caedus, the murder of Mara Jade, the Galactic Alliance Guard's wartime crimes, and the Battle of Shedu Maad. Background context for the novel — the war that produced the Foundation, the Vigil, Tess, Korda, and Talon's ruin.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Characters reference it directly ('the war', 'during Caedus', 'before Shedu Maad'); the formal name appears only in narration when needed for clarity.

terminology_registry.definition: The decisive engagement at the close of the Second Galactic Civil War in 40 ABY. Darth Caedus was killed; Jacen Solo's death; the war ended. Site of significant casualties on both sides. The Memorial Foundation takes its name from the post-war reconstruction of these losses.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Characters refer to it as 'Shedu Maad' (the battle) and to the planet as 'Shedu Maad' (the Jedi HQ); context disambiguates.

terminology_registry.definition: OUT-OF-UNIVERSE reference — the 2013 Troy Denning novel that establishes Luke/Leia/Han's Mortis-adjacent metaphysical encounter and effective retirement. Used here ONLY in canon documentation; characters do NOT reference 'Crucible' on-page.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: On-page, characters reference 'what happened two years ago' or 'after the Aramatak business' or simply notice Luke's quieter manner without naming the event. Mortis is NEVER named on-page.
